title: Adult chest compressions should be:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Adult chest compressions should be:
options: 5-6 cm deep at 100-120/min, with full recoil
8 cm deep at 150/min, on the upper sternum
body.explanation: Lower half of the sternum, minimal interruptions, firm surface.

title: A palpable radial pulse suggests a systolic pressure of at least about:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: A palpable radial pulse suggests a systolic pressure of at least about:
body.explanation: Femoral about 70, carotid about 60 mmHg.

title: Agonal gasping in an unresponsive person should be considered:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Agonal gasping in an unresponsive person should be considered:
options: A seizure that needs no CPR
body.explanation: Start CPR if unresponsive with absent or abnormal breathing.

title: In trauma, the airway is managed with:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: In trauma, the airway is managed with:
options: Head tilt and full neck flexion
body.explanation: ABCDE with cervical spine protection.

title: Shock may develop when blood loss exceeds about:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Shock may develop when blood loss exceeds about:
body.explanation: Check for hidden bleeding, including under the patient.

title: Normal adult intracranial pressure is:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Normal adult intracranial pressure is:
body.explanation: Raised ICP is 20 mmHg or more.

title: The compression-to-ventilation ratio for adult CPR is:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: The compression-to-ventilation ratio for adult CPR is:
body.explanation: Untrained or unwilling rescuers can give continuous compressions.

title: The Monro-Kellie doctrine states that:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: The Monro-Kellie doctrine states that:
options: In a fixed skull, an increase in brain, blood or CSF volume raises ICP unless another decreases
ICP depends only on blood pressure, because the skull can expand to absorb any change in volume
body.explanation: Every ICP treatment works by reducing one of the three volumes.

title: The three aims of first aid are:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: The three aims of first aid are:
options: Diagnose, treat and discharge the victim
Preserve life, prevent worsening, promote recovery
body.explanation: Care given before professional help arrives.

title: Before approaching a victim, the first responder must:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Before approaching a victim, the first responder must:
options: Start CPR immediately, even before checking the scene
Secure the scene and ensure their own safety
body.explanation: Self-control and safety come first; use PPE against body fluids.

title: The first step to control external bleeding is:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: The first step to control external bleeding is:
body.explanation: Then wound packing, then a tourniquet for massive limb bleeding.

title: When splinting a fracture you should:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: When splinting a fracture you should:
options: Immobilise the joint above and below and check neurovascular status before and after
Straighten an open fracture by force
Immobilise only the fracture site, after straightening the limb by force
body.explanation: Cover open wounds with dry sterile dressings.

title: Cerebral perfusion pressure equals:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Cerebral perfusion pressure equals:
body.explanation: Autoregulation keeps flow stable for CPP of about 60-160 mmHg.

title: A tourniquet is indicated for:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: A tourniquet is indicated for:
options: Massive, life-threatening limb bleeding when direct pressure fails
Any bleeding that soaks through a first dressing, including nosebleeds
body.explanation: Wide, flat band (7.5-10 cm), never wire or rope; note the time.

title: A tourniquet should be placed:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: A tourniquet should be placed:
options: As close above the wound as possible
Below the wound, over the nearest joint
body.explanation: Twist until bleeding stops.

title: In the primary survey ABCDE, 'D' stands for:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: In the primary survey ABCDE, 'D' stands for:
body.explanation: Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, Exposure/Environment.

title: Sudden cardiac arrest is most often due to:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Sudden cardiac arrest is most often due to:
options: Ventricular fibrillation or pulseless ventricular tachycardia
Atrial fibrillation with a fast ventricular rate
body.explanation: These shockable rhythms are why early defibrillation matters.

title: A pelvic sling should be centred on:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: A pelvic sling should be centred on:
body.explanation: Remove belts and pocket items first.

title: The 'three Cs' are:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: The 'three Cs' are:
body.explanation: Once the scene is safe.

title: Removing a motorcycle helmet is absolutely contraindicated if:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Removing a motorcycle helmet is absolutely contraindicated if:
options: There is neck pain or paraesthesia during removal, or an impaled object
The helmet is a full-face model and the victim is conscious and cold
body.explanation: Otherwise it should be removed pre-hospital for airway care.

title: The Moroccan emergency (SAMU) number taught in the course is:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: The Moroccan emergency (SAMU) number taught in the course is:
body.explanation: Give an exact location when calling.

title: In a young athlete, sudden cardiac death is classically due to:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: In a young athlete, sudden cardiac death is classically due to:
options: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or anomalous coronary origin
Coronary atherosclerosis or a pulmonary embolism
body.explanation: Coronary disease dominates in older people.

title: The AED should be attached:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: The AED should be attached:
options: As soon as it is available
Only after a pulse check of 1 minute
body.explanation: Early defibrillation is a key link in the chain of survival.

title: At a road accident you should NOT:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: At a road accident you should NOT:
options: Use the hand brake and block the wheels of the damaged vehicles
Try to right a vehicle lying on its side
body.explanation: Stabilise it only if safe and trained.

title: Health professionals should check for a pulse for no more than:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Health professionals should check for a pulse for no more than:
body.explanation: In doubt, start CPR.
